top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, removing Doppler, recoil and light-shift limits), demonstrated by Katori and brought to the 10^-18 regime by Ye, and reproduced across independent laboratories. It is already used to measure things (centimetre-scale geodesy, gravitational redshift, bounds on constants), and Katori and Ye is the cleanest two-name attribution on the table, with seven of eight members supporting it. P002 is a fair fallback on discovery grounds but has unresolved credit gaps (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, 3D work) and overlaps the 2016 prize. A prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Mentor-lineage link only: during my PhD I spent a year in John Hall's laboratory, and Hall was Ye's mentor; no collaboration, co-authorship or funding with Katori or Ye. Disclosure rather than recusal appears appropriate; I also run the spin-off Deep Light Vision, unrelated to any candidate.
